chapter: Radio color line, San Francisco and Columbia staff
title: No other black musician on staff; Lionel Newman and Benny Carter
summary: Lee says no other black musician joined the Columbia staff, and Benny Carter declined a Fox composer-arranger offer from Lionel Newman.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Right. But anyway, I'm just saying, ever since I can remember, the closest anyone came to being on the staff was Lionel Newman was very fond of Benny Carter, you know -- very fond of Benny Carter. And when Benny Carter had his big band down here -- you know, Benny used to do a lot of work at 20th Century Fox, and they wanted him to come off the road with the band and wanted to give him a job there as a composer and arranger.

Oh yes, because Lionel Newman -- you know, times had changed, and Lionel Newman -- you're talking about a different individual, you know. He was also very talented person and he saw so much in Benny Carter, you know, he is a tremendously talented man; he's a multi faceted man; he plays trumpet and saxaphone, but he is a exceptionally good writer. A lot of people didn't realize, you know, how well he could write, but he is a good writer, and a good composer.

But he didn't take that, because he was still too much in to his horn, still too much in to the big band thing. So I think I stayed there until probably '47 and then -- when did I get together with ...
